subject: Biotechnology
title: Cell Therapies
description: Learn Cell Therapies in one minute.

hook.text: Living cells as medicine — not a molecule in a vial but billions of cells infused into the patient.

buildup.text: Mesenchymal stem cells dampen inflammation — clinical trials target graft-versus-host disease and osteoarthritis.

discovery.text: iPSC-derived cells could provide unlimited supply — one donor's cells reprogrammed to treat thousands of patients.

twist.text: Living drugs are unpredictable — cells can migrate, multiply, or change behavior inside the patient.

climax.text: Allogeneic off-the-shelf cell therapies avoid patient-specific manufacturing — freezer-ready doses for immediate use.

punchline.text: Cells that heal, not just chemicals that treat — living medicines.

quiz.question: What is the advantage of allogeneic cell therapies over autologous?
options: They use the patient's own cells, ensuring perfect compatibility
They are manufactured in advance from donor cells, available immediately off the shelf
They work only for blood cancers, not solid tumors

details.summary: Cell therapies use living cells as therapeutic agents, including CAR-T cells for cancer, mesenchymal stem cells for inflammation, and regulatory T cells for autoimmunity. Each patient's cells may be engineered ex vivo and returned, creating a living drug.
details.whyItMatters: Cell therapies have produced remarkable cancer remissions in patients who exhausted all other options. They represent medicine's frontier of using living, adapting therapeutic agents rather than static chemical or protein drugs.
takeaways: Cell therapies use living cells as therapeutic agents that adapt and persist
CAR-T cells have achieved durable remissions in blood cancers
Manufacturing each patient's cells individually creates cost and logistics challenges

faq.question: What types of cell therapies are currently approved?
faq.answer: Six CAR-T cell products are FDA-approved for blood cancers including leukemia, lymphoma, and multiple myeloma. Several stem cell therapies are approved for blood disorders. More cell therapies for solid tumors, autoimmune diseases, and heart failure are in clinical trials.

faq.question: Why are cell therapies so expensive?
faq.answer: Each treatment is individualized: a patient's cells are collected, shipped to a facility, genetically engineered, expanded for weeks, quality-tested, and shipped back. This personalized manufacturing costs hundreds of thousands of dollars per patient with no economies of scale.
